title: In the beginning was the Word (John 1:1–5)
hookLine: the light shines in darkness and the darkness did not comprehend it

lines: MARK: A VOICE IN THE DESERT.
cards: Matthew starts with a family tree. Mark starts with a man shouting in the desert. Luke starts with an old priest in the temple.
John starts before anything started. No Bethlehem, no shepherds, no Jordan River. Just: in the beginning.
Those are the first words of the whole Bible, the opening of Genesis, before light, before land, before anyone. John borrows them on purpose.
For the next six weeks we read the fourth Gospel in order, and on day one it reaches back past the first day of creation.

teach.b: Here's the opening, in the Douay-Rheims: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." Today's word is John's, logos.
In Greek it means a word, but also reason, an account, the meaning behind things. Greek philosophers had used logos for the order running through the universe.

Jewish readers knew of God's word that creates, and of Wisdom, who was with God at the making of the world. John takes all of that and says something none of them said: the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

teach.h: ALL THINGS WERE MADE BY HIM.
teach.b: Then: "All things were made by him: and without him was made nothing that was made." Not a star, not a cell, is outside him. In him was life, and the life was the light of men.

teach.h: THE DARKNESS DID NOT COMPREHEND IT.
teach.b: "And the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it."
Comprehend is a lovely double word: understand, and also grasp, get hold of. The darkness didn't understand the light, and couldn't get hold of it either.
Translators have argued for centuries which John meant; many think both.
Saint Augustine remembered the old priest Simplicianus telling him that a Platonist philosopher used to say these opening lines deserved to be written in letters of gold and set up in every church.
On Christmas Day the Church reads them at Mass, so the baby in the manger is heard with this first: before Bethlehem, the Word.

how: Catholics hear John's prologue at the Mass of Christmas Day, and again on the Second Sunday after Christmas where that Sunday is kept.

games.q: you're writing a fourth life of Jesus. the others began with a family tree, a desert prophet and a temple priest. where do you begin?
o: with his baptism in the Jordan.
games.why: John begins in the beginning: the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and all things were made by him.

practice: If you can, turn off the lights and light a candle or one small lamp, or simply picture it, and watch how the dark doesn't push it out, and how far one small flame reaches.
Let the line come back slowly: the light shineth in darkness. If you pray, rest in that line; if you don't, stay with the flame and the dark around it.

wordCard.voice: Logos. Greek for word, reason, meaning. John's name for the one who was with God in the beginning, and who was God. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: word, reason, account, meaning. John's name for the Son in John 1:1.

carryVoice: Your line: the word was God. A beginning older than Bethlehem. Day four hundred ninety-two.
